title: Elastic attention-density split + kernel-aware scheduler for prefill/decode
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem statement: Current prefill/decode scheduler uses fixed phase split heuristics (prompt vs decode) tuned for average sequence shapes. For workloads with heavy attention sparsity or short-lived KV reuse we see suboptimal kernel choices and either wasted GPU cycles (throughput loss) or increased tail latency for latency-sensitive tenants.

Goal: Implement an elastic split policy that adaptively chooses: 1) phase split granularity (microphases vs standard prefill/decode) based on a lightweight attention-density signal, and 2) kernel selection routing that favors sparse-attention kernels when density below threshold and dense kernels otherwise. The policy should preserve tenant fairness and latency SLOs while improving overall token throughput and reducing CPU/GPU kernel thrashing.

Approach:
- Add an attention-density estimator in the prefill stage that samples attention patterns from the first N tokens (configurable, default N=8) and produces a density score (0..1).
- Map density -> split granularity: density < 0.2 -> microphase split with sparse-kernel preference; density 0.2-0.6 -> hybrid split with kernel probe; density > 0.6 -> standard two-phase prefill/decode with dense-kernel path.
- Kernel-aware scheduling: the scheduler will consult per-kernel latency profiles (recent rolling 5-minute stats) and estimate end-to-end token latency when routing to sparse vs dense kernels including expected KV cache and batching impacts.
- Fairness: integrate with tenant crediting so microphase-heavy workloads consume proportional slot credits; add soft-degradation (fallback to dense kernel) for tenants nearing credit exhaustion.
- Safety: feature-flagged rollout plus canary on dedicated pools; automatic rollback if p95 latency increases > 20% for flagged tenants.

Acceptance criteria:
- Experimental cluster shows >=8% tokens/sec uplift on mixed-sparsity synthetic workload with no more than 5% p95 latency regression for latency-tier tenants.
- Tail latency (p99) across observed production traffic does not increase by more than 10% during a 48-hour canary.
- No increase in kernel thrash metric (kernel-switches/sec) beyond 15% for steady-state traffic.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: full model-architecture rewrite for attention-sparsity-aware kernels, billing changes, or multi-region routing.

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Experiment build: shippable binary and runtime flag, internal perf job on canary clusters (engineering only).
2) Canary: enable for 5% of tenants on dedicated pools for 48h. Collect latency, throughput, kernel-switch metrics.
3) Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% if metrics meet guardrails.
4) Postmortem and docs update.

Design docs & artifacts: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/elastic-attn-density-splitter (design draft), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4567 (prototype PR), https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-tests/pull/102 (benchmark harness), Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/rt-scheduler/elastic-split-experiments

notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive microphasing reduces per-token latency variance for sparse attention but increases kernel-switch overhead and may reduce batching efficiency. We intentionally probe kernel latencies before fully committing to a route to reduce oscillation. Long-term we may integrate model-architecture signals (sparsity priors) and move decision to compile time. For now we keep decision runtime and conservative to avoid regressing dense workloads.
